programme: SKI acting as a SMAD-pathway corepressor (its target SMAD7 marks it as a direct TGF-β/SMAD antagonist) together with SMARCC1, a core BAF/PBAF SWI/SNF subunit (its own target list includes the paralogous subunits SMARCB1 and SMARCA4, confirming complex membership) — i.e. a TGF-β-signalling / SWI-SNF chromatin-remodelling axis, not a generic 'immune' or 'cancer' label.
role_in_a: In Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma, SKI attenuates canonical TGF-β/SMAD growth-restraint to accelerate tumour progression (PMID 30972853), and SMARCC1 expression tracks pathological grade and prognosis (PMID 33532313), consistent with the SWI/SNF (BAF/PBAF) complex being a defining altered pathway in ccRCC biology more broadly.
role_in_b: In Multiple_sclerosis, TGF-β signalling and SWI/SNF-dependent chromatin remodelling are independently established as controllers of CD4+ T cell fate (pathogenic Th17 versus regulatory Treg differentiation) that underlie CNS autoimmune demyelination — but the specific MS-tagged papers retrieved for SKI and SMARCC1 do not confirm this mechanism for these two genes: the SMARCC1 paper (PMID 36335117) is mechanistic about SWI/SNF complexes without a stated MS link, and the SKI paper (PMID 38767415) concerns thymic epithelial cells with no MS mention in the text shown.
shared_axis: TGF-β signal strength, set by SMAD-corepressors like SKI and executed through SWI/SNF chromatin complexes containing SMARCC1, is a lever both tissues are known to depend on independently — tumour cells use it to escape growth restraint, CD4+ T cells use it to set pathogenic-versus-tolerogenic fate — rather than a documented, disease-specific link between ccRCC and MS.
reasoning: Both carrying factors are independently and directly placed in Kidney_Clear_Cell_Carcinoma by retrieved papers (SKI/TGF-β antagonism, SMARCC1/grade correlation), and TGF-β-SWI/SNF control of T cell fate is well-established general MS/EAE immunology, so the programme is real in each disease separately. But nothing retrieved connects either factor to MS specifically — the MS-tagged papers for both were flagged by the reader as unclear or off-topic — so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about a generic pathway, not on retrieved evidence, capping this at moderate rather than strong.
support: PMID 33532313 - SMARCC1 expression correlates with pathological grade and favorable prognosis in renal cell carcinoma; PMID 30972853 - SKI (c-Ski) accelerates renal cancer progression by attenuating TGF-β signalling; PMID 36335117 - mechanistic SWI/SNF-complex paper retrieved for SMARCC1 in MS, but no clear MS connection stated in the text available; PMID 38767415 - thymic epithelial cell paper retrieved for SKI in MS, but MS is not mentioned in the abstract snippet shown.
how_to_falsify: In ccRCC lines, deplete SMARCC1 (BAF155) and ask whether SKI-repressed TGF-β/SMAD target loci (e.g. SERPINE1, CDKN1A, SMAD7 itself) lose the expected chromatin-accessibility/SMAD-occupancy changes when SKI is also depleted — if SMARCC1 loss has no effect on SKI-dependent TGF-β target regulation, the proposed SWI/SNF-SMAD cooperativity does not hold in this tumour. For MS, profile SKI and SMARCC1 expression and SMAD7-locus chromatin state across naive versus EAE-induced pathogenic Th17 CD4+ T cells (or MS patient PBMC subsets); no differential expression or binding during pathogenic polarization would falsify the proposed shared axis in MS.
caveats: Brain|kidney is an anatomically distant tissue pairing, so any shared programme has to work through a generic signalling pathway rather than local tissue identity. 390 patient-group comparisons across 6 independent cohort pairs give solid recurrence statistics (SKI and SMARCC1 concordant in 164/390 and 179/390, i.e. 42% and 46%, not the top of the list), but per the record's own summary no factor has direct literature evidence in both diseases, and 7 of the 12 listed factors (L3MBTL1, KLF12, HINFP, SIX4, PATZ1, ELK3, PLAGL2) have no usable evidence in either disease and are not part of this account. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed classic autoimmune/neuro regulators (FOXP3, STAT4, TCF4, MEF2C, ASCL1, etc.) that would otherwise be the obvious way to narrate an MS connection — their absence here is by design, not a gap to fill in. POU2AF1, DACH1 and BHLHE40 also carry direct single-disease evidence (MS and ccRCC respectively) but were excluded from the programme because they do not mechanistically link to the TGF-β/SWI-SNF axis carried by SKI and SMARCC1; a different, equally partial story could be told around them instead.
